identity.real_world_identity_notes: Ligier Automotive specifies the JS P217 with a Hewland TLS-200 six-speed sequential gearbox and semi-automatic pneumatic steering-wheel paddle shift. AMS2 exposes one exact model identity in two class contexts: LMP2 for Gen2 and LMP2_Gen1 for Gen1.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit checks in both AMS2 class generations showed the same closed GT/Formula rim with an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, both AMS2 class generations moved from rest without physical clutch input. The simulator mechanism was not established, so this record states only the user-facing requirement and does not claim a verified real-world automatic or anti-stall clutch.
Both generations exposed six paddle-selected forward gears and accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts without driver lift.
Automatic cut was perceptible on upshifts in both generations.
Both generations accepted clutch-free downshifts with the driver's foot off throttle, and automatic blip was directly visible as a throttle-display spike.
Gen2 emitted class LMP2; Gen1 emitted class LMP2_Gen1. Both emitted the exact model identity Ligier JS P217.
Gen1 and Gen2 were live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Both class contexts confirmed six paddle-selected gears, no-lift clutch-free upshifts with automatic cut, clutch-free downshifts with automatic blip, and the same GT/Formula display rim.
Physical clutch input was not required to move from rest, but the underlying simulator mechanism was not determined.

confidence.basis: Exact identities and the full user-facing control technique were directly checked in both AMS2 class generations; the manufacturer independently establishes the gearbox hardware.

claims.basis: Official addition plus exact live CarModel, CarId, LMP2 Gen2 class, and LMP2_Gen1 class observations through SimHub 9.11.22.
Constructor specification and direct exercise of all six paddle-selected forward gears agree.

Both class generations directly demonstrated clutch-free move-off, no-lift clutch-free upshifts with perceptible cut, and clutch-free downshifts with a visible automatic-blip throttle spike. The unknown mechanism behind move-off is explicitly not inferred.
Direct cockpit inspection in both class generations showed the same closed GT/Formula display rim.

notes: One record covers both explicitly observed AMS2 class contexts because their exact model identity and tested controls are the same.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "prototype", a value that named a racing category rather than a rim outline. That value is retired: the rims it covered are the same closed form, flattened at both the top and the bottom, that the project now records as "gt-style". The shape was remapped by definition and the rim was not observed again.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
driver_summary: Hewland TLS-200 six-speed sequential with pneumatic paddle shift, to Ligier's own specification. No clutch to pull away, and the car cuts and blips for itself.
